findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the S3 stale-clone forced-override MECHANISM in the proof: how staleness (>N days) is detected on reconnect, how the clone is forced to `reset --hard` to the rewritten remote instead of taking the documented diverged/unrelated-history union-merge path (docs/concurrency.md sync algorithm), and how this suppresses re-introduction of pre-rewrite commits — reconciling the accepted >N-day loss with the standing non-destructive-recovery invariant (WS3 fix).
evidence: Plan C3: 'stale clones (> N days) forced to reset to remote (no reintroduction)'; S3: 'stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect'

docs/concurrency.md sync algorithm (lines 714-727): the 'diverged' branch runs `merge origin/tickets (union)` and 'never reset', and the unrelated-history branch also merges-as-union keeping every local commit — UUID-named event files 'never collide', so a stale clone's pre-rewrite commits/trees would be RE-INTRODUCED on reconnect

docs/concurrency.md 729-746 (WS3 fix): reset --hard was removed precisely because it orphaned local commits; the model is now non-destructive union recovery — a forced reset is a direct reversal of that invariant and needs its own mechanism + proof

A rewrite makes the stale clone's merge-base the OLD history, so absent a specified override the standing algorithm re-adds exactly the objects the reclaim removed and resurrects retired events (violating C3)
findings.finding: S3 asserts stale clones are 'forced to reset to remote (no reintroduction)' but does not specify the override MECHANISM, which conflicts with the documented reconvergence model that never resets a diverged/local-ahead clone and would union-merge the pre-rewrite history back in.
findings.location: Mechanism S3 / Design C3 / Acceptance criterion 'S3 stale-clone override enforced on reconnect'
scenarios: A clone drifted >N days with unpushed writes reconnects after the ref swap; its next read/write triggers reconverge, which sees divergence and union-merges the pre-rewrite commits back onto the reclaimed branch
The reclaim's object-count win is silently undone as one stale clone re-pushes old history

findings.checklist_item: Specify how writes from fresh (<N-day) clients committed during the write-fence / between backup and swap are fenced, drained, or replayed post-swap (and how rollback recovers them), so the dual-write window causes no lost writes beyond the explicitly-accepted stale-clone case.
evidence: Plan: 'live clones with unpushed writes need a write-fence/maintenance window' names the hazard but not its handling
Plan: 'non-FF force-update of a shared, auto-pushed, high-write-rate branch'
The accepted-loss clause covers only '>N-day-drifted clone's divergent work'; fresh-clone writes during the window are a distinct, unaddressed case
Rollback restores 'refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<date>' which predates any in-window writes
findings.finding: The dual-write window during cutover is named but not handled: fresh (non-stale, <N-day) clones with unpushed writes committed during the write-fence/maintenance window, or between the backup-ref snapshot and the force-swap, have no specified preservation or reconciliation path — and rollback to the pre-reclaim backup ref would also lose them since the backup predates them.
findings.location: Risk / rollback section; Acceptance criteria (S2, S3)
scenarios: A developer on a current clone pushes a ticket mutation during the maintenance window; the force-swap overwrites it and rollback cannot recover it
Reconciler auto-push fires between backup snapshot and swap
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC that defines the write-fence protocol (quiesce auto-push, snapshot the backup AFTER the fence engages, and replay/reconcile any fresh-clone writes captured during the window post-swap), plus a DATA LOSS RISK note distinguishing in-window fresh-clone writes from the accepted >N-day stale-clone loss.
